proposals.before: His grandfather Jiang Zhan served in the Song as Left Director of the Bureau of Honors and as a Three Ministers of Equal Court Rank.
proposals.after: His grandfather Jiang Zhan served in the Song as Left Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and as Equal in Ceremonial to the Three Ministers.
proposals.reason: 左光祿大夫 is a prestige court title, not director of a Bureau of Honors; 儀同三司 marks ceremonial equality with the Three Ministers.

proposals.before: His father Jiang Nian was a Composition Official and was killed by Liu Ziye (Emperor Taichu).
proposals.after: His father Jiang Nian was a Composition Official and was killed under Taichu.
proposals.reason: Chinese 太初 denotes the Taichu era associated with Liu Shao in AD 453, not Liu Ziye.

proposals.before: When Prince Guiyang of Xiufan assumed his provincial post, he invited Xiao to serve as Master of Reception, but Xiao declined.
proposals.after: When Liu Xiufan, Prince of Guiyang, assumed his provincial post, he invited Xiao to serve as Master of Reception, but Xiao declined.
proposals.reason: 桂陽王休範 is Prince of Guiyang, personal name Xiufan; the English reverses title and name.

proposals.before: He was soon made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on Prince Ancheng's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.after: He was soon made Attendant-in-Ordinary on Prince Ancheng's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.reason: 驃騎從事中郎 is a cavalry-staff post, not an attendant of the Masters of Writing.

proposals.before: Earlier, Jiang Zhan had married a daughter of Chu Xiu and was later dismissed; when Chu Yuan became General of the Guard, he admired Xiao's character, opened relations with him in advance, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
proposals.after: Earlier, Jiang Zhan had married a daughter of Chu Xiu, who was later sent away; when Chu Yuan became General of the Guard, he admired Xiao's character, opened relations with him in advance, and appointed him Chief Clerk.
proposals.reason: 被遣 refers to sending away the wife, not dismissing Jiang Zhan from office.

proposals.before: He was then made Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the staff of the Grand Marshal.
proposals.after: He was then made Attendant-in-Ordinary on the staff of the Grand Marshal.
proposals.reason: 太尉從事中郎 is a grand-marshal staff post, not Masters of Writing.

proposals.before: At the start of the Yongming reign he again served Prince Yuzhang as Adviser to the Grand Marshal and Recorder, then became Companion to Prince Nanjun and Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling of Jingling.
proposals.after: At the start of the Yongming reign he again served Prince Yuzhang as Adviser to the Grand Marshal and Recorder, then became Companion to Prince Nanjun and Secretary on the staff of Prince Jingling.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic English repeats the fief name as “Prince Jingling of Jingling”; the Chinese has only 竟陵王.

proposals.before: The emperor's mind was then released.
proposals.after: The emperor's anger then subsided.
proposals.reason: Literal “mind was then released” for 上意乃釋 is unidiomatic and obscures that the emperor’s displeasure was allayed.

proposals.before: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and also served as provincial Director of Selection for his native commandery.
proposals.after: He was promoted to Palace Attendant and also served as provincial Director of Selection for his native province.
proposals.reason: 本州 is the native province, not a commandery; the literal field already has “province.”

proposals.before: When Prince Jian'an of Xiuren held Yang Province in the Song, he recruited Chang as provincial Master of Records.
proposals.after: When Prince Jian'an, Xiuren, held Yang Province in the Song, he recruited Chang as provincial Master of Records.
proposals.reason: 休仁 is the prince’s personal name, not a place; “Prince Jian'an of Xiuren” reverses the relationship.

proposals.before: When Prince Jianping of Jingsu served as Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou, Chang again became his Master of Records and was esteemed for his longstanding integrity.
proposals.after: When Prince Jianping, Jingsu, served as Northern Expedition Commander for Southern Xuzhou, Chang again became his Master of Records and was esteemed for his longstanding integrity.
proposals.reason: 景素 is the prince’s personal name, not a fief; “Prince Jianping of Jingsu” misreads the name as a place.

proposals.before: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was reassigned as Director of the Secretariat and then as tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was reassigned as Director of the Palace Library and then as tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
proposals.reason: 祕書監 is the Palace Library directorate, not the Secretariat (門下/中書).

proposals.before: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was changed to Director of the Secretariat and then changed to tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
proposals.after: When Emperor Ming took the throne, Xiao was changed to Director of the Palace Library and then changed to tutor to the Prince of Jin'an.
proposals.reason: The same 祕書監 error appears in the literal English.

proposals.before: The late emperor treated him with affection, and the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or commoners in the countryside, though their knowledge differed in detail, who did not know what had happened?
proposals.after: Emperor Shizu treated him with affection, and Emperor Taizong regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or commoners in the countryside, though their knowledge differed in detail, who did not know what had happened?
proposals.reason: 世祖 and 太宗 are Song temple names for the emperors who favored Prince Jianping; Founding Emperor mistranslates 太宗 and collides with 太祖 later.

proposals.before: The Former Emperor was intimate with him, the Founding Emperor regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or humble men in the wilds, though what they heard and saw differed, who did not know this affair?
proposals.after: Shizu was intimate with him; Taizong regarded him with special favor; whether court nobles or humble men in the wilds, though what they heard and saw differed, who did not know this affair?
proposals.reason: Literal English likewise renders 太宗 as Founding Emperor, which is 太祖 elsewhere in the chapter.

proposals.before: He sought release from Xuzhou to avoid the crucial post at the northern gate; he bitterly begged for Kuaiji, eager to dwell in the idle duties of eastern Yong—this all is manifest in the record of deeds.
proposals.after: He sought release from Xuzhou to avoid the crucial post at the northern gate; he bitterly begged for Kuaiji, eager to dwell in the idle duties of eastern Ou—this all is manifest in the record of deeds.
proposals.reason: 東甌 is Dong'ou, the eastern seaboard; Yong is an unrelated toponym and contradicts the idiomatic eastern frontier.

proposals.before: At the start of Jianping there was obstruction, and in Yuanhui there was not yet open rebellion—the aim was solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only deepened the suspicion against the prince.
proposals.after: At the start, Jianping met obstruction, and in Yuanhui there was not yet open rebellion—the aim was solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only deepened the suspicion against the prince.
proposals.reason: 建平初阻 refers to Prince Jianping's early obstruction, not a Jianping reign period; Yuanhui is the era name.

proposals.before: At the beginning of Jianping there was obstruction; in Yuanhui there was not yet rebellion—one wished solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only increased the suspicion incurred.
proposals.after: At the beginning Jianping met obstruction; in Yuanhui there was not yet rebellion—one wished solely to lay blame on Ruan and Yang, which only increased the suspicion incurred.
proposals.reason: Same misreading of 建平 as a reign in the literal line.

proposals.before: The Founding Emperor praised his integrity and made him Recorder, then promoted him through Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
proposals.after: The Founding Emperor praised his integrity and made him Recorder, then promoted him through Western Left of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Attendant of the Palace Secretariat, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
proposals.reason: 司徒 is Minister of Education/Masses, not Minister of Works (司空), which is Chu Yuan's office in s0075.

proposals.before: The Founding Emperor praised his righteousness, transferred him to be Recorder, promoted him to Western Left of the Minister of Works, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Palace Secretariat Attendant, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
proposals.after: The Founding Emperor praised his righteousness, transferred him to be Recorder, promoted him to Western Left of the Minister of Education, Attendant of the Household Bureau on the Grand Marshal's staff, Palace Secretariat Attendant, and Chief Clerk on Wang Jian's Guard staff.
proposals.reason: Literal line repeats the 司徒/Minister of Works error.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang petitioned to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar to the prince, and they drew together in purity and trust with deep mutual affection.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongming, Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, petitioned to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar to the prince, and they drew together in purity and trust with deep mutual affection.
proposals.reason: 竟陵王子良 is the Prince of Jingling, given name Ziliang; of Ziliang treats the given name as a place.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongming, Prince Jingling of Ziliang memorialized to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar for Prince Jingling; through purity and trust they won each other, and their affection was very deep.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongming, Xiao Ziliang, Prince of Jingling, memorialized to establish Companions and Academy officers; Chang was made Literary Scholar for Prince Jingling; through purity and trust they won each other, and their affection was very deep.
proposals.reason: Same inversion of title and given name in the literal English.

proposals.before: When Prince Linhai of Zhaoxiu held Jing Province, Chang was made his Chief Clerk, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, with charge of Jing Province affairs.
proposals.after: When Liu Zhaoxiu, Prince of Linhai, held Jing Province, Chang was made Chief Clerk of the Western Central Commandant, General Who Assists the State, and Administrator of Nanjun, with charge of Jing Province affairs.
proposals.reason: 昭秀 is the prince's personal name, not a place; 西中郎長史 is omitted in the idiomatic rendering.

proposals.before: Yao had four elder brothers—Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong—and the world said that Xie Zhuang had named his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
proposals.after: Yao had four elder brothers—Yang, Fei, Hao, and Chong—and the world said that Xie Zhuang had named his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
proposals.reason: 朏 is Fei, not Tiao; the given name matches the Moon semantic series.

proposals.before: Yao had four elder brothers Yang, Tiao, Hao, and Chong; the age called Xie Zhuang's naming of his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
proposals.after: Yao had four elder brothers Yang, Fei, Hao, and Chong; the age called Xie Zhuang's naming of his sons Wind, Moon, Scenery, Mountain, and Water.
proposals.reason: Same romanization error for 朏 in the literal field.

proposals.before: On entering office he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.after: On entering office he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant Gentleman on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.reason: 從事中郎 is an adjutant post on the Rapid Cavalry staff, not an office of the Masters of Writing.

proposals.before: On leaving the sackcloth he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant of the Masters of Writing on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.after: On leaving the sackcloth he became Secretary Attendant and rose to Attendant Gentleman on the Founding Emperor's Rapid Cavalry staff.
proposals.reason: Same invented Masters of Writing in the literal rendering of 驃騎從事中郎.

proposals.before: He was soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: He was soon made Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and General of Valiant Cavalry, then regular concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: 長兼侍中 is regular concurrent Palace Attendant, not Chief Clerk.

proposals.before: Soon he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then Chief Clerk and concurrently Palace Attendant.
proposals.after: Soon he was transferred to Junior Mentor of the Heir Apparent and concurrently General of Valiant Cavalry, then regular concurrent Palace Attendant.
proposals.reason: Same mistranslation of 長兼侍中 as Chief Clerk.

proposals.before: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement."
proposals.after: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose; Yao alone remained seated and said, "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—yet Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own achievement."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works (司空/工部).

proposals.before: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Minister of Works Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power."
proposals.after: Later at a court banquet, when meritorious ministers offered wine, Director of the Imperial Secretariat Wang Yan and others rose from their seats; Yao alone did not rise and said: "Your Majesty received the mandate, responding to Heaven and following the people—Wang Yan presumptuously claims Heaven's merit as his own power."
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works.

proposals.before: When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Ministry of Works, hoping to win him over.
proposals.after: When the banquet ended, Yan invited Yao to ride back with him to the Directorate of the Imperial Secretariat, hoping to win him over.
proposals.reason: 令省 is the office of the 尚書令, not the Ministry of Works.

proposals.before: When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the Ministry of Works, wishing to soothe and please him.
proposals.after: When the seating ended, Yan called Yao to ride together back to the office of the Director of the Imperial Secretariat, wishing to soothe and please him.
proposals.reason: 令省 is the Shangshu ling's office, not the Ministry of Works.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongtai he was made Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongtai he was made Regular Cavalier Attendant and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 散騎常侍 is Regular Cavalier Attendant; Scattershot Cavalry is a false calque.

proposals.before: In the first year of Yongtai he was transferred to Regular Attendant of the Scattershot Cavalry and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.after: In the first year of Yongtai he was transferred to Regular Cavalier Attendant and Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
proposals.reason: 散騎常侍 is Regular Cavalier Attendant, not Scattershot Cavalry.

proposals.before: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was in Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said: "In this there is only what suits drinking wine."
proposals.after: Earlier, when his elder brother Tiao was taking up the post at Wuxing, Yao saw him off at Zhengliu Ford; Tiao pointed at Yao's mouth and said: "In this there is only what suits drinking wine."
proposals.reason: Chinese 爲吳興 marks appointment to Wuxing, not merely being already stationed there; the farewell at Zhengliu Ford is a departure scene.

proposals.before: He was a younger cousin of Wang Yan, Minister of Works.
proposals.after: He was a younger cousin of Wang Yan, Prefect of the Masters of Writing.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is the director of the imperial secretariat, not 司徒/Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Prince Jianping of Jingsu in the Song recruited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with great respect.
proposals.after: Jingsu, Prince Jianping of Song, recruited him as Master of Records for Southern Xuzhou and treated him with great respect.
proposals.reason: 景素 is the personal name and 建平王 the title; 'Prince Jianping of Jingsu' reverses that relation.

proposals.before: Because his cousin Wang Yan was Minister of Works, Siyuan did not wish to hold a key inner-court post alongside him and submitted a firm memorial declining the appointment.
proposals.after: Because his cousin Wang Yan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Siyuan did not wish to hold a key inner-court post alongside him and submitted a firm memorial declining the appointment.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is Director of the Imperial Secretariat, not Minister of Works (司徒).

proposals.before: Because his cousin Yan was Minister of Works, Siyuan did not wish to hold together with him key posts in the inner administration and submitted a firm memorial of declination.
proposals.after: Because his cousin Yan was Director of the Imperial Secretariat, Siyuan did not wish to hold together with him key posts in the inner administration and submitted a firm memorial of declination.
proposals.reason: 尚書令 is mistranslated as Minister of Works.

proposals.before: Yet I would rather seek punishment and abandon wealth and glory—what a fool would do, and what I too hope to avoid.
proposals.after: Yet for me to court punishment and throw away wealth and glory is something even a fool would not do, and I too hope to avoid it.
proposals.reason: 愚夫不爲 means even a fool would not act thus; the idiomatic English reverses the negation.

proposals.before: Even so, after they had left he still ordered two men to sweep each other's brooms over the place where they had sat.
proposals.after: Even so, after they had left he still ordered two men to ply brooms over the place where they had sat.
proposals.reason: 交帚 is using brooms together, not sweeping each other's brooms.

proposals.before: He spoke for his former lord, his words born of righteousness.
proposals.after: He Changyu spoke for his former lord, his words born of righteousness.
proposals.reason: Chinese 何 is the surname of the biographical subject He Changyu, but the English reads as a pronoun and drops the name.

proposals.before: He spoke for his old lord; his words arose from righteousness.
proposals.after: He Changyu spoke for his old lord; his words arose from righteousness.
proposals.reason: Chinese 何 is the surname He, not an English pronoun; the literal line should keep the named subject.

The combined title “Prince Jianping of Jingsu” exists only in the inverted English; the Chinese supplies the title 建平王 and the personal name 景素 as separate claims c0439 and c0438.
